subject: CareGrid MAP: deployment commitment statement + sprint cadence
messages:
From: Sam Reynolds <sam.reynolds@caregrid.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@caregrid.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CareGrid evaluation / MAP kickoff

Jordan — thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can lock dates: 

1) Decision drivers: data residency for PHI (US-only), p95 latency target under load (<= 450ms), and predictable monthly spend for budget sign-off.
2) Evaluation window: CareGrid wants a two-week functional POC running real inference on 10M monthly tokens equivalent.
3) Preference: they'd rather avoid on-prem for now; leaning between Hosted with VPC peering or a Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) depending on cost differential.

Can you send a short MAP that includes (A) success criteria, (B) procurement milestones (quote, legal, PO), and (C) a go/no-go date? Also attach any SOC2 evidence artifacts we can share with their compliance team.

Sam
Director, Solutions — CareGrid Health

Attachments: (none in this message)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Reynolds <sam.reynolds@caregrid.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: CareGrid evaluation / MAP kickoff

Sam — appreciate the succinct list. Draft MAP attached (CareGrid-MAP-v2.xlsx) and a redwood SOC2 summary (SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf). High-level proposal below so we can align on dates: 

- Success criteria (POC pass):
  * p50 latency at 256 tokens <= 180ms; p95 <= 450ms on expected QPS (25 qps steady, 150 qps burst).
  * Semantic parity: automated evals and 50 hand-label prompts with <2% quality regression vs baseline model.
  * Security: VPC peering + KMS-managed keys for logs and model payloads; SOC2 artifacts reviewed.
- Evaluation plan (two-phase):
  1) Week 1 (smoke + perf): small hosted sandbox with prefix caching enabled; run 1M token baseline tests and latency profile.
  2) Week 2 (load + parity): Dedicated reserved pool candidate (warm) to compare unit cost and tail latency under sustained load; parallel eval harness for quality checks.
- Decision matrix: cost delta (hosted vs dedicated) + tail latency tradeoff + compliance gating. If hosted meets p95 & cost within 15% of dedicated estimate -> choose Hosted with reserved burst. If dedicated provides >=20% cost savings or needed isolation -> Dedicated. Private (on-prem) remains fallback if procurement requires full control.
- Proposed procurement timeline:
  * 2027-05-18: Redwood sends formal quote and MAP workbook (we will).
  * 2027-05-21: CareGrid legal sends security questionnaire back / redlines.
  * 2027-05-28: Executive go/no-go (internal CareGrid).
  * 2027-06-04: Target contract signature + PO via procurement.

Next steps: Marissa, can you attach the MAP workbook with the milestones (I added notes in the sheet) and Karthik — can you confirm we can provision a dedicated pool for the Week 2 window and estimate cost delta by Monday?

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0199

Attachments: CareGrid-MAP-v2.xlsx, SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CareGrid evaluation / MAP kickoff

Jordan / team — quick feasibility notes after checking infra calendar and cost models: 

- We can stand up a Dedicated pool for the Week 2 window (NVIDIA A10G-equivalent nodes) and isolate CareGrid via tenant reservations. Provisioning lead time: 48–72 hours once we have PO + whitelisted CIDR for peering.
- Cost delta estimate: Dedicated reserved (monthly pro-rated) looks ~27% cheaper per-token for their projected throughput vs pure Hosted on-demand. With our reserved burst plan (hosted + burst to dedicated), delta narrows to ~8% but gives them lower operational friction.
- Latency: Dedicated pool should reduce p95 tail by ~80–120ms in our benching under sustained QPS due to fixed GPU capacity and reduced multi-tenant jitter.
- Data residency / compliance: VPC peering + KMS keys in customer-managed AWS account is supported for both Hosted (private peering) and Dedicated modes; Private (on-prem) would need extra ops time (estimate 6–8 weeks).

Risks / asks:
- Need their security contact to sign an NDA/SSP access this week so we can share granular SOC2 docs (we can provide redacted logs and architecture diagrams).
- Confirm expected token mix (short vs long sequences) so we can size KV cache and batching appropriately — Sam / Maya, can you share a sample distribution?

I will push a cost worksheet into the MAP sheet and flag an exact number by EOD Monday.

Karthik
Director, Infrastructure Solutions — Redwood Inference

Jordan / team — thanks for the quick turn. A few confirmations and a tweak to timeline after internal procurement sync: 

- Security: We will sign the NDA and send the SOC2 questionnaire responses by Tuesday EOD. Our security lead (Maya) is copied.
- Token mix: roughly 70% short (<=64 tokens), 25% mid (65–512), 5% long (>512). We'll drop a CSV sample into the MAP folder.
- Timeline tweak: procurement requested a hard decision by 2027-05-26 (internal exec review on the 25th). If that works for you, can we accelerate the cost worksheet and schedule the Week 1 sandbox for 2027-05-19 -> 2027-05-21 and Week 2 dedicated window 2027-05-24 -> 2027-05-27?

If Redwood can confirm Dedicated provisioning + cost numbers by 2027-05-18 morning, we can aim for the 25th internal review. Otherwise we'll need to roll. Also please flag any contract terms that usually add days (data processing addendum, indemnity).

Sam
